ajadapramatrsiddhi:ajad-p01: Just as there is no difference between the real and the unreal in their own nature, so too — this is certain — there is no such difference between the inert and the non-inert. Appearing (prakhyā) and describing (upākhyā), existence and its opposite, non-existence — none of this touches a thing's essence; that essence is what faces the knower. Nor can a thing's very self be "being an object of appearing and describing" — for that would make it depend on something else, give it no single form, and break past existence itself. Granted, let there be no difference; still, from the presence and absence of appearing, a difference does get established here — and that much serves the purpose. Even so, existence would only be fitting as tied to appearing; without reference to that, existent and nonexistent are indistinguishable. But how could they be indistinguishable here, when the existent performs a function (arthakriyā) and the other does not? And yet the thing, in its own self, remains without distinction. So the existent thing, having taken on the limiting condition of appearing-as-functional, would exist by its own essence — yet it is not distinguished from the nonexistent. But even there, function is not what is described in a thing whose existence is already established; the two are exactly on par — hence their grounding rests on consciousness. And if consciousness itself were of the form of non-grasping (aparāmarśa), then it too, in itself, would be exactly equal to the inert non-being, as before.
ajadapramatrsiddhi:ajad-p02: If she — by her become self-nature — has never won final grounding, how could she become the standing-place of establishment for another existent? Consciousness, apt to ground another thing's showing by saying 'this,' would take that grounding nature — and again, by itself, by saying 'I.' For certainty — by exclusion and inclusion both — is called the fixed order, the foundation, the attainment, the completion of the other, inert selves. So these inert ones, near-unreal in themselves, belong to shining alone; shining alone is — of its own self, through selves both own and other. And there is no experience apart from distinct-and-indistinct certainty — apart from connected shining, grasp-less in its self. For this 'this'-grasping, cut off, fulfillment is rest in its own form — and that grasping, 'I am this,' is this itself. Twofold is this same self: measured and unmeasured — by breath and the rest restrained, an atom; as supreme self, unbroken. For both, this is the end-ground of all object-awarenesses — one alone through continuity. So no other is possible. And in the I-knowing whose self is non-separation grasp, limit-dwelling — nothing inert beyond shining appears.
anubhavanivedana:anu-p01: When the yogin abides with mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim — he, seeing yet not seeing outside with unmoving-pupil gaze — this indeed becomes the śāmbhavī mudrā, by your grace, O guru: devoid of void and non-void becomes that reality, the śāmbhava state.
anuttarastika:anu-p01: Transition here is no method at all — not contemplation, not speech-connection, not discussion, not visualization, not steadying, not japa-practice-effort. So what is well-decided? Speak the supreme truth, and hear it: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying.
bhairavanukarana:bhair-p01: Oṃ. Obeisance to Consciousness-Bhairava. You who shelter in consciousness-ground: take consciousness-state, wander not in vain. Proclaiming thus — Śiva, bent on grace, conquers for devotees. Consciousness-Bhairava alone — supreme, supreme-nectar-formed, one, high-blazing. All swallowed by the ring of shining faculties — Śiva I venerate. Praised, praiser, praise — though distinct, nothing is here. It endures: as whatever form, by consciousness-form, so becomes this. All-distinctions-melted, all-distinction-self, consciousness-mass-bliss — which Your principle, Lord — its imitation, Your form — I venerate. Outline-man, man, letter-script, letter-mass — just as, just so, of varied form, You — shape reveals, supreme self. There concept-free indeed — You consciousness-formed entered — we reflect: what even a bit? Not indeed principle fancy's-object. Own-light made, speech-goddess, sense-flowers-offering-arranged — first-unfolding guru, then venerated, heart entered. I praise, reflecting, the Great Lord — self, own, consciousness-one-mass. Poured-out-bond-cluster — in this body-god-house. Consciousness-bliss-will-cognition-action-named powers conquer, O Lord. Having got subtle-gross splits — mouth-hood, Brahma-skull-named. Omniscience-objected, heart and the rest, six-limbed — Yours. All up to Sadāśiva — by corpse-self — Your seat, O Lord.
bhairavastava:bh-p01: Pervading the particular states of moving and unmoving — consciousness-made, one, endless, beginningless: Bhairava-Lord, refuge of the helpless — by mind become Yours, in heart I venerate.
bodhapancadasika:bod-p01: Of unsetting sun-light is His form — of bright powers and of darknesses too. For He is one, within, and powers and darknesses end in Him.
bodhavilasa:bodh-p01: Oṃ. Salutation to Netra. Salutation to Śiva constantly — maker of the five acts, manifest as supreme-self bliss. Consciousness is free, the universe's cause — so called; freedom-formed, the knower — and powers too she bestows. She — on her own ground, by her own will, for the world's unfolding — from varied fit variety, from subject-object difference. That world's variety stands through object-difference — manifold-variety-yoked, high-and-low-numbered. From consciousness-tightening comes mind — though knower, even the great Lord. Like a banyan seed, there the world-form — that the wise know. Knowing is the self's pure form — stainless, utterly stainless. That same, rule-bound, is called mind — knowing. Object-faced, awareness has come to rest in mind. From tightening-dominant-self, the wise know knowing as mind. The māyā-knower, knowing-formed, one with that, abides among embodied beings — clinging to objects, void of true discernment. Ever one, the established mind — by kalā, sattva, guṇa and the rest, by seven-knowerhood, by thirty-six count. One, everywhere, pure, awareness-selfed, the great Lord. From mis-knowing that I-ness, freedom sits in the palm.
ipvv:chunkA-svatyandya:
**The spontaneity of the Lord: the self-aware light**

This is where the whole Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī begins — with the spontaneity, the
svācchandya, of the Lord. And the doctrine is announced in its fullness from the first lines. The blue
and the yellow and the jar are not things that a light shines upon from outside; they shine forth
*as* the light, without abandoning their own being, and are one with the manifestation itself. This —
that the world shines as the consciousness, and that the consciousness shines as the world — is the
Lord's spontaneity.

The Lord is of the nature of consciousness. He shines forth as the whole variety of knowers and knowns,
with a body that appears as if it were more than consciousness even though it is not more; and — this is
decisive — he is *aware* of shining. The image Abhinavagupta uses is the mirror. A mirror reflects the
wall, the house, the elephant, the horse, the person, the pot, the potter — all the distinctions of
part and whole, support and supported, cause and effect — without being more than its own smooth
surface. But the mirror does not know that it reflects. That is its only limit; it is inert. The Lord
is the mirror that *knows*: he shines forth as all things, and he is aware that he does so, because
consciousness culminates in reflexive-awareness. The light that shines is the light that knows itself
shining.

And this answers the obvious objection: "then it would always shine." For the "always" has no
independent time against which it could fail. What we call time is just the sun's movement — the
shining of things in their succession. To ask "why does the world shine as the sun moves?" is like
asking "why does the blue not shine as yellow?" It is the nature of the light to shine; there is no
time outside it that could make it shine or not. So the Lord is: *śaśvat*, un-cut by time; *acchanna*,
never becoming other than his own form; *svaccha*, clear — able to appear as more than himself while
being only himself; and *svacchanda*, spontaneous — free of all dependence on another, resting in his
own pulsation.

And so the opening of the work is a prostration. The author bows to Śiva — the param-eśvara who removes
the delusion of the world, who is the essence of all good, the bliss and the liberation. And the
prostration, Abhinavagupta explains, is not an empty word. It is the samāveśa, the entry: the
abandoning of the bound knower's conceit, the subordination of the "I" of the world, and the rising of
the self-aware consciousness. Even the word "namaḥ," the bowing, does its work not by being offered as
a bare sound but by pleasing the Lord — as the oblation's svāhā kindles the flame and gives to the
deity.

So the whole teaching is here, in the first opening: the Lord is the self-aware light, the mirror that
knows, the spontaneity that shines as the world and is aware of shining; and the recognition of this —
the entry into this self-aware Śiva — is the whole of the liberation the work will unfold.

---
isvarasiddhi:isva-p01: The maker — him, I praise, the one God, Maheśvara the Lord. Bodies and the rest have conscious cause, distinct-arranged — pots … like atoms. Conscious-urged — or … […] as pot from [tha]t. … devoid of locus-form. Fixed is its meaning in place — in that action-heaped … In the varied, the conscious alone is marked — as among pots. The maker, wise, resolved on varied use. There is, in function-yoking, among bodies and worlds, this distinct array — never from mere matter. Here then — conscious makers proved, the Lord's act proved: for such-variety-knowers, lordlessness is impossible. Neither potter nor Lord shows agreement here — for him, opposition would follow, or agreement unproved. Merely showing pervasion with the conscious alone — by thesis-force, somewhere, someone wise is understood.
kramastotra:kram-p01: This is the completion-rite amid sorrow's host — in the spreading taste of great bliss-essence, this foul day: for by mutual doing, in the hymn of the Lord, weighty with scorching uneven flames, the mind constantly reflects back — its fear gone.
pancashloki:pan-p01: Whatever I have truly done, O Lord — no duty of mine goes beyond this: my pride, laid at Your lotus feet with devotion. This is my all; I know there is nothing other. So, casting all else aside — quickly, O protector of the helpless, O ocean of compassion — be pleased with me!
paramarthacarca:par-p01: Distinct from the illumination of sun, moon, lamp and the rest, it does not shine — on account of over-pervasion; and hence: of the nature of light, just this much — illumined-illuminator named is mere convention.
paramarthasara:param-p01: I resort to You, Śambhu — supreme, beyond-abiding, beginningless, one, cave-entered manifoldly, abode of all, abiding in all moving and unmoving: to refuge. Whirled in the sorrow-wheel from womb-dwelling to death-ending, the student asked the blessed Lord, the support: the supreme truth. By support-verses the teacher addressed its essence to him; Abhinavagupta tells it by Śiva-teaching-view-yoga. By own-power-glory-weight, this fourfold egg in division: power, Māyā, nature, earth — thus manifested by the Lord. Therein within, this universe is a varied body-faculty-world continuum; and therein the enjoyer, embodied, is Śiva indeed, fettered-state-taken. As the stainless crystal assumes the form of various sorts, so the Lord too holds god-man-beast-plant form-ness. As water moves and the moon-disc moves, as water stills so stillness goes: so this self, the great Lord, in the body-faculty-world mass. As invisible Rahu, abiding on the moon-disc, shines, so the all-going self, by resorting to objects, shines in the mind-mirror. As a face shines in a dirt-free mirror, so this self shines, light-formed, in the mind-principle purified by Śiva's grace-descent. Light-formed, complete, great-bliss from resting in own self, filled by will, knowing and acting, endless-power-complete.
parapravesika:par-p01: Veneration to Śiva, whose very self is all the levels of reality. Here begins the Entering-into-the-Supreme, composed by glorious Kṣemarāja, noblest of the great Māheśvara teachers. We bow to consciousness itself — the heart of the supreme Lord — which has the world for its form and yet goes beyond it, pulsing in the shape of supreme power.
paratrimshika:para-p01: Tell me this secret of secrets, Lord — the Power that dwells in the heart, Kaulinī, mistress of the clan. I tell it, no doubt: swift Kaula-fruition. This Kaula rite, Goddess, abides in my heart-sky. First now: all lunar days, vowels ending in the drop; within them, by time's conjoining, moon and sun are declared. Realities from earth to person, in five groups in order — in the ka-series and the rest, ending with the ma-sound, O fair-vowed one. Fourfold the stations of wind, fire, water and their lords; above them the famous śa-series, and before, the five Brahmas. Rootless, in due order, to be known, ending in kṣa — this forthgoing declared; of all mantras and wisdoms indeed, O glorious one. This is the womb, ever told in all Tantras — joined with the fourteen and the tithi-lord's end; the third brahma, fair-hipped, the heart of Bhairava himself.
paryantapancasika:pary-p01: Filled with rest of beginning-end-entered endless power — unspeakable — I study speech: the Lord's heart. He indeed Bhairava god; all gods of-whom-made. That very Bhairavī — being, non-being too — of-whom-made. That indeed Bhairava's knowledge-ignorance too of-whom-made. He indeed Bhairava-doctrine — opponent too of-whom-made. Unity of six paths — where that Bhairavī abides — at the end of all systems — ineffable, supreme goal. She — bliss-only-self-merged will-knowledge-true-action — heart of god-of-gods, of Bhairava, undivided ground. From nature of consciousness, that god by own self reflecting — Lord, from unattached to end-of-stages — stages attains. There expressive, expressed, self — of two vibrations singly — of Lord gross, subtle, supreme appearance — of sequences sixfold path.
phrdaya:phr-p01: Consciousness stands free — cause of the world's proving. By her own will, on her own ground, she opens the world. That grows manifold through fit perceivers and perceived dividing. A contraction of knowing, yet a knower even so, clothed in a contracted world.
ptvmadhyama:ptvm-p01: O Lord, what is the Unsurpassable that grants Kaula fruit at once — known by a mere touch of knowing, rising to kinship with the Sky-Goer? Tell me this secret of secrets, Lord — the Power that dwells in the heart, Kaulikī, mistress of the clan. Tell me of her, Lord of gods, by whom I come to fullness. — Hear, blessed Goddess: even the answer has one beyond it — the Unsurpassable. This Kaula rite, O Goddess, standing in my heart-sky — I tell it, O lady of gods: it gives swift Kaula fruit. First now: all lunar days, vowels ending in the drop; within them, by time's conjoining, moon and sun are named. Realities from earth to person, in five groups in order — in ka-series, in sounds, ending with the ma-sound, O fair-vowed one. Fourfold the holds of wind, fire, water and their lords; above them, śa beginning the famed row, and before, the five Brahmas. Rootless, rightly ranged, to be known, ending in kṣa — this forthgoing declared; of all mantras indeed, and of wisdoms, O glorious one. This is the womb, told in all Tantras in every way — joined with the fourteen, O lucky one, joined with the tithi-lord's end; the third godhead, O fair-hipped, the heart of Bhairava himself.
saktavijnana:sakt-p01: Place, entry, form, and mark, and sign indeed; raising, awakening, and wheel-rest indeed — and the arrival at the stage, and the final state indeed; rest, transformation, and the return indeed — and So the doctrine is thirteenfold: the supreme Śākta wisdom, pointed out in every Trika treatise by Śambhu himself. Five fingers below the navel, two fingers above the member — between them lies the place called the bulb, remembered as the station of the wheel. Hold the breath in and out, and cast the mind right there; master the currents of wind completely, and lead them until they enter the middle. This — they say — is entry. Now I will tell the form: a wheel like a horned pond, six-spoked, and steady beyond. The bulb glows like a pomegranate blossom, red by its very nature; this form is declared the third — it consists of contemplation. Set the mind in that middle until it stands steady there; when the wind's hold is released, point out the mark. In the middle of the bulb-wheel stands a digit of the unstruck sound, ringed with lines above and below, coiled like a serpent. Above and below abides her state — sun and moon both; truly she shines, bright as a thousand suns.
sambandhasiddhi:samb-p01: With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference — by whom all things are proved, whose work is world-traffic — him, Śiva, by own will, we praise. Dawning by a body made of relation through being, difference, and the rest — conquering though one: the world-self, light, the supreme Lord. Awaiting and dependence are no relation for the two inert ones: impossible — even where selfhood is won, they are metaphor, not definition. From the teaching that non-beings obtain selfhood, two-seatedness too is abandoned: form-fusion alone thus stands as relation's meaning. Not uninterruptedness — for it misses relation: if it were so, it would hold of iron bars. Hence fusion of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood. No barring of the many in one's very oneness, others say: things unmixed in themselves — thought joins them. Since this is no mere thought — it cannot be dismissed: like the snake-error, it resists remedy by clinging to a shining. Since clinging to a shining is not a thing resembling a shining but a following after shining — error is exactly that: a shining astray. Thus even in this shining, the many's unity-seeing has a statable warrant — declared plainly in recognition's path.
sivasutra:sivs-p01: I bow to that whose opening and closing make the worlds dissolve and arise — to him, source of the power-wheel's glory, Śaṅkara. Where this whole effect abides, and whence it has come forth — from being uncovered in form, there is no obstruction anywhere. Even in waking and the rest, in difference, it glides in the undifferent; the perceiver-ness never turns back from its own being. I happy, I suffering, I attached, and the like — those awarenesses plainly abide elsewhere, strung on pleasure-states. Where there is no suffering, no joy, no graspable, no grasper, and not even delusion — THAT is, ultimately. Since the sense-host, deluded, thinks itself undeluded — forthgoing, standing, dissolving, by the inner wheel. By that effort the to-be-examined reality is got respectfully; since its freedom is everywhere unmade.
spanda:span-p01: By whose opening and closing the worlds dissolve and emerge — to him, source of power-wheel glory, I praise Śaṅkara. Where this whole effect abides, and whence it has come forth — from being uncovered in form, there is no obstruction anywhere. Even in the difference of waking and the rest, it glides in the undifferent; the perceiver-ness never turns back from its own being. I happy, suffering, attached, and the like — those awarenesses plainly abide elsewhere, strung on pleasure-states. Where there is no suffering, no joy, no graspable, no grasper, and not even delusion — THAT is, ultimately. Since the sense-host, deluded, thinks itself undeluded — forthgoing, standing, dissolving, by the inner wheel.
spandasandoha:sand-p01: He alone — Śiva, possessing spanda, self-established — who makes the inner face taste. This hero, lord of the Kula — victorious.
stavacintamani:stav-p01: Who, grown great with the wealth of glory, compassion, awakening, and supreme bliss, his greatness lit by knowledge — he conquers, the undefeated. To the forth-flowing drop and resonance, to the self made of pure nectar: bow; to endless light, to Śaṅkara, the milk-ocean. You we hate, you we hymn, with you we counsel — O Ambikā’s lord: lightly won, how good — the whole world you have borne for us. To the yoked withdrawn touch, to the full-streamed nectar, to the sky-and-māyā-formed: to the vast one, to Śambhu — bow. Among the split, not split; among the cut, wholly uncut — we bow to that all-common form of the supreme Lord. Subtler than praṇava's upper half-mora — to the minute, and again to the great; vaster than the world-egg — to the qualified-by-qualitylessness, to Sthāṇu: bow. The world-egg-bearing one — of the sky-pervading, of the all-going, of the supreme-Lord-goose — that power, goose-like, we praise. With no provision of material, on no wall at all, they spread the world-picture — bow to him, the art-praised trident-bearer. From māyā's watery belly fully drawn out and made stainless — Śiva-knowledge, milked of itself: give, come, O Hara-goose, to us. Even in the yoga of six-valid-means' delimitations and difference: to the undivided; to the one being of ultimate truth — an offering we bring, to Bhava, to you.
svabodhasiddhi:svab-p01: Bow to the giver of freedom, made of every blessing — to Śiva, the sun that burnt away the darkness on every road of becoming. I praise the highest Śiva — sick with no possession by any creed, to be known only by the feeling of the self, dwelling in himself. Bow, let there be bow, to Śambhu — smasher of the net of fancies and their floods, standing past even the highest bliss. Victorious are Śambhu's feet: they teach the wandering world to tell the real from the sham, and wake the knowledge that frees. Mind, thought, ego, breaths, the senses' subtle fuel and life — all turn back when they see the one worth worshipping, whom we worship. I bow — I — to pure awareness: the only knife that cuts the heart's knot of 'mine' and 'I', that swallowed throbbing and its stillness both.
tantraloka-a02:tal-a02-p01: Now the first word, of unceasing highest-recognition-nature: to determine it, this second treatise I begin. For the means-less, whose nature: what point by teaching here? Once may teaching be; afterwards as means-less it is called. This means-less reality — whence without means? By itself; but of them that such: what should we say, indeed, to them? Which fourfold-told form of awareness — of the pervading, this: own nature alone is to be regarded; for ever-arisen is the pervading. By so many uncounted natures it shines; some part-by-part, others enter partlessly through that. There too, from means-and-the-rest-expecting otherness-yoga, of means too not to be barred: variety from its otherness. There, who pure-souled, in Bhairavī, own awareness, means-less practicing: whose rule — is proclaimed. There, for now, rite-yoga does not deserve means-hood; for from that arisen, rather it is distinctly discerned. In awareness, means just would be — quoted; if awareness is called: luminosity in self-luminous — and that, thence, from another — how? Awareness-principle, 'self-luminous' — in this, what? Now, by reasoning: in its absence, would the universe be non-shining from inertia?
tantraloka-a05:tal-a05-p01: By the individual means and its rule, this is determined for those who desire the supreme abode. When conceptualization is purified and the desired thing is unopposed, attainment of enjoyment and liberation is certain. Conceptualization becomes very stable when it arises from one's own self-freedom, without dependence on other means. For someone, conceptualization directed toward self-purification is said to depend on other means, according to the previous rule. Conceptualization is called the nature of pure consciousness; though situated, it still joins freedom for the limited self. Certainty is manifold, and the means there are distinct; they are spoken of by the word anu according to far and near. Ultimate truth shines in intellect, breath, body, and cognizer, even in what is non-ultimate. Because it is non-different from pure consciousness light, that body of inert and conscious is doubled through freedom. In Traishirasa it is said to the goddess: the individual soul is Shiva's power, situated everywhere. Established in realization of one's own nature, supreme through unfolding knowledge, consciousness-nature is true through conception of freedom's expansion.
tantraloka-a07:tal-a07-p01: Now this supreme secret, the rising of the cakras, is told. Thus effortless spoken; effort-born but is described: seed-syllable-natured all, of consciousness vibration-nature. Bringing supreme consciousness means thus described, like waterwheel machine bucket flow. By single concentration effort wonderful machine-rising should obtain; by single concentration force arisen in mantra-rising night. That mantra-deity by effort-identity becomes pleased; in sky taste-one-eye in eternal-rising, half of that in two-seed-lump. In three seven thousands two-hundred thus rising held; in four but thousands five and indeed four-hundred. In five-syllable ocean-thousands three-hundred twenty so; in six three-thousands six-hundred rising would be. In seven three-thousands but six-eighty-excess remembered; by hundreds but by twenty-seven in eight-syllable variation. By twenty-four hundreds but in nine-syllable rising would be; by sixty-one-twenty of hundreds in ten-syllable. Nineteen hundreds sixty-four in Śiva-syllable; eighteen hundreds would be rising in twelve-syllable.
tantraloka-a11:tal-a11-p01: The path of art will be spoken according to glorious Shambhava knowledge. As in the previously stated middle of the world, after each group follows its own, a separate principle is said to be called. Thus, among those principles too, that which is of the nature of approach to its own class and separated from the other class is called kala in the teaching of Shiva. Some say that this power, again, is the very subtle power within the principles; it is called kalā, as the bearer in earth. Here the thing does not appear divided in two alternatives, because a universal is not accepted as following, unlike the Nyāyikas and others. Others say that at the beginning of initiation, for the purpose of easy collection, Shiva devised a class called kala, which is samaya-dependent. The covenant made by the God of gods does not reach ultimate reality; yet it is not false, and no other covenant arises. Cessation belongs to the earth-principle, establishment to the manifest perceptible domain, knowledge to the end of night, and peace to the end of power; this egg is four. In the Shiva-principle beyond peace, supreme Shiva is beyond kala; here there is no classification, convention, or even counting. It is united in all directions in the abode of the expansion of freedom; but from freedom its own form does not fall away from the nature of the knower.
tantraloka-a12:tal-a12-p01: Now the use of this path, our present subject, is set forth. Thus this whole path, as it rests in consciousness, through that rests also in void, intellect, breath, channel-wheels, and bodies. And outside too, everywhere in liṅga, image, fire, altar and the rest; so it stands, whole and part-wise, in sequence and all at once. Laid out from consciousness-principle to the outer, this path: at each level one should make one's own form shine, by own freedom, in fitting form. And everything's form everywhere — even his does not not shine; for we cannot bear exclusion anywhere, even in dream. Thus one should behold the body as filled with the universe-path, painted by time's activity — the abode of pulsation made of space and time. So beheld, he is made of the deities within the universe; to be meditated, worshipped, libated — entered then, one is freed. Thus pot, cloth, liṅga, altar, book, water — or whatever one may see anywhere: there one should reach identity-with-that. Therein offering of things is held worship through non-difference; and contemplation of full-formedness is called meditation.
tantraloka-a14:tal-a14-p01: Now the nature of concealment, as it is told, let it be examined: from own nature the Supreme Lord touches the rule-bound and rule-free order. Touching, he shines forth; thereby he is called self-willed: having resorted to the rule of action and fruit — this Great Lord. He ordains creation, preservation, destruction — the intermediate states; and again, in the great creation, in the endlessness of creation and destruction. One, that God, universe-self, the Lord arrived at abandoning rule; and whatever intermediate creation — and stasis here too is unforced. He does not abandon the form; niyati-abandoned, standing here: that. But by niyati alone, when, through the self-concealing procedure. He enjoys suffering, delusion and the rest; then the action-fruit order — but having abandoned the karmic restraint, enveloped in suffering-delusion. Desiring to shine forth, sits this one, in concealment disregardful; as from light's freedom, the awakened like the unawakened. So sits, uncrossed yet as-if-crossed, behaving; as the awake one her fool-conduct performing even while hating it. In the heart sits the fool — thus indeed of the awakened is the conduct; and the venerable Vidyā-lord said, in the Mānastotra, such as this. Who on your teaching-path, initiated, falling through delusion into dissent: surely of them there is not your sun-appointment — can lotuses contract from sunbeams?
tantraloka-a17:tal-a17-p01: Then I speak the procedure that bestows identity with Bhairava-nature, thus in five: mandala, pot, fire, disciple, and self. Having taken unity of pervasion, one places the path and the student's course; the three impurities—karma, māyā, and anu—are placed on the arm, on the throat, and likewise. And the teacher should cast into the crest by thread-knot union; its appearance as other than its own form is impurity; that knot is called impurity. For the firmness of the reply 'iti,' an external knot is arranged; the arms are the seat of action; the Vishnu-maya self dwells in the throat. Thus imagination, made from the downward-flowing flame-atomicity, produces manifoldness in the triad called nara, shakti, and shiva. To speak, one should arrange a ninefold thread for knotting; fire, water, and food are threefold, each in three ways. At the end of hearing, some from this entered the white, black, and red; then in fire, having satisfied all mantras, they became consciousness-space only. In the common form of the principles, one should practice gradual purification; there, by union with one's own mantra, one should first invoke earth. Having worshipped with flowers and the like, one should then propitiate with ghee, sesame, and the like the deity pervading each principle, and afterwards the presiding deity of the māyā principle. Having invoked and worshipped maya-shakti with one's own mantra, one should satisfy it; the matrika syllable is used in invocation, and the malini syllable in worship.
tantraloka-a18:tal-a18-p01: Now this concise initiation is taught — the attainment of Śiva-hood: no powder-mandala, no eve-rite here, no taking of ground and field; but in whatever place, the guru worships Śiva. Having meditated the path with the mind, the knower of the tattvas' far shore should initiate her who is freed from birth and the rest — by whatever path the guru proceeds. He should make it ending in the single tattva, steeped solely in the Śiva-mood; then with the Parā-mantra unto him: 'Now I purify the tattva.' 'Svāhā' thus for each tattva; upon purification he should cast the full oblation. So with all other mantras too — or else as told. Enclosed with Parā by name, ending in svāhā, ending in the first: a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred-and-eight — with that, with śakti indeed, he should offer. Then 'pūrṇā' — having purified the unbroken, highest, such-like — the initiation-rite taught here and there in scripture by the Great Lord.
tantraloka-a19:tal-a19-p01: Now the initiation giving immediate departure is set forth: from that moment, or from enjoyment, at body's fall one may go to Śiva — so hinted in the Mālinīśāstra by the Great Lord. At body's fall, when death is near, from śaktipāta's clearness, having obtained Śāṃkara initiation: hence from the initiation-moment, the supreme. The meaning 'may go to Śiva' was explained here, from prior-posterior discernment, by our venerable guru Śambhunātha. When death is near and śaktipāta arises, there, in mild cases, by guru-service life may go to diminution. Or else, through kin-friends-and-the-rest, the Omnipresent's [grace] falls; or before, the samayin has not at all obtained supreme initiation. Even the initiated, desiring to abandon life-breaths, freed from affliction: the final guru should then perform immediate-departure initiation. But not in immature impurity, nor even in remaining-karmic-body, should departure be performed: so set forth in the venerable Gahvara. Having seen the disciple age-seized, oppressed by disease, having made depart, then he should join this one in the supreme principle. In the qualifier-qualified relation, from desire-conduct-arrangement, the aforesaid things were here set forth by venerable Śambhunātha. Having performed all the aforesaid rite, from samaya-purity, he should place his blazing marma-scissors knife.
tantraloka-a20:tal-a20-p01: Now I speak the initiation that brings confidence to the deluded.
tantraloka-a21:tal-a21-p01: Now the initiation-rite of the one situated in absence is described. For accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation one is led to the true guru: in this Mālinī sentence 'prati' is expressive of facing-towards. Facing-towards of the disciple consists in becoming the seat of his grace; the saying 'worshipping him' is an indicator of the cause of grace. From that connection then someone is liberated instantly: thus is also the meaning of this jewel of the Mālinī sentence. 'In that instant' means there is no further moment of desire to approach; but exactly thus the guru, struck by compassion, should uplift him. Of one who, body wasted by guru-service, died without obtaining initiation — or whose desire arose at the moment of death. Or of one who shared the initiation-rites of lower tantras etc., having obtained samaya-status, (but) not having obtained the supreme initiation. Of one struck by a ḍimba, or devoured by a yogeśī through sorcery, or slain by yantra-tantra etc. by the guru — the dead. Of one who, having obtained initiation, violated his samaya — even so, through the vehement entreaty of relatives, wife, friends, sons. Or by itself, by the force of compassion arisen towards that person even, (of one) who is the bearer of a portion of śaktipāta come towards him known.
tantraloka-a22:tal-a22-p01: Now the so-called liṅga-lifting we speak: solely enjoined in the Śiva-teaching. Told in the venerable Mālinītantra, indeed: the earth-upholding — having declared, who is yoked where, he from it does not turn back. Arisen from fitness, whose just where the teaching: he just there is to be appointed; at initiation-time, then, but this one. Fruit, all, having attained, in Śiva: though yoked, released; though unyoked, upper purification, having attained from Bhuvaneśa. Purified, he comes to Śiva-hood, burnt-saṃsāra-bonded; having declared man-upholding — and told, this Vedāntic, by me. To Kapila formerly told, in the first chapter, so: by this, through sequential yoga, attained — the highest state. Not again to beast-hood goes: in the pure own self he stands; hence, for, is hinted the meaning — this, even for those below the Śiva-principle. In the principles, of the yoked there is re-extractability: of the giver of all-śāstra-taught thing-distinctions. Of the Śiva-āgama is distinction than all — even — āgamas; and through Śiva-knowledge, without, again even beast-arising. And the sequence: śakti-descent, impurity-loss, departure-desire, initiation, awakening, abandonable-loss, acceptable-dissolution-nature.
tantraloka-a23:tal-a23-p01: Then the rite of consecration is told by the supreme Lord. This rite, spoken in putraka initiation, is for guru and sadhaka too; it is entitled and endowed with knowledge of bhogya-tattva, in due order. Having known him to be a well-practiced knower, a being desiring to become a future one, and fit, the guru should confer his own authority to him. Whoever does not know thus is not even consecrated; the teacher is set out by the order of samaya and the rest, as said in the glorious Kāmika. He who does not know the sixfold path-union, situated externally and internally, is not a guru who releases, according to the Siddhayogīśvarīmata. Even one who lacks all marks, if he possesses knowledge, is regarded as a guru; thus knowledge-primacy is indeed stated in Sri Kacabhargava. The guru knows words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge; is solely devoted to Shiva; understands the meaning of all Shiva scriptures; and is compassionate. The Supreme Lord himself states the characteristic of the self-born: the non-devotee whose thought is fixed on mere living, though he acts under Īśāna's control, is not (self-born). One born from a later self is self-born but not entitled; nor is the mere "sprout of ash" entitled anywhere, nor the son of a vow-keeper, nor likewise the son of bad character. Kuṇḍa and gola are wicked; this is said in the Devyākhyayāmala; and one reborn with another gender is again established in Śaiva.
tantraloka-a24:tal-a24-p01: Now hear the secret final sacrament taught in the Śāmbhava teaching. For all from lower stations up to gurus, clearly: after the aforesaid śaktipāta one should perform the funerary initiation. And for followers of the upper teaching whose selves are samaya-struck, the funerary initiation is to be performed by the tattva-knowing guru. For him who stumbled through negligence into samaya-conduct faults, the funerary initiation is to be done — so in the venerable Dīkṣottara teaching. Whatever was told before in the rite called corpse-uplifting — that entire procedure here, on the corpse-body, he should perform, there on the image. This rule told in the Siddhātantra is set forth: what would be last, making that last first and first last. Having withdrawn each oblation, the funerary rite is held twofold — but not so for the sādhaka whose samaya is bathed in worship, meditation, and mantra. From the body's fall this one is freed, or becomes a sky-rover, dear lady; when the tattva-accomplished teacher has died, wherever it be.
